title: A joint drift fit weakens the step correction of 1982-2022 DOISST warming
abstract: We tested how gradual difference drift changes the mean-step correction of DOISST v2.1. We used 492 regional monthly values from a signed prior study and three references. Five fixed-date steps can absorb 84.8 percent of a pure linear drift with no jumps. At 60 S to 60 N, removal of the fitted steps gives 0.128-0.144 C per decade if smooth drift is excluded, but 0.151-0.165 if a linear drift is allowed; raw DOISST gives 0.171. Local four-year fits still give positive global steps in 2005 and July 2020 against all three references. Thus local jumps do not fix their total long-term trend effect. The east-Pacific adjusted point estimates stay negative in all nine tested fits, but all linear-model correction-only intervals include zero. At 50-60 S even the adjusted point estimate changes sign with the reference. We give exact design checks, paired block intervals, local checks, code and fit tables. The result is conditional on fixed dates and simple drift models. It reuses one prior extraction and does not identify which product has gradual error.

display.caption: Adjusted trends under three smooth difference models. Pointwise 95 percent paired residual intervals use 24-month blocks. All dates are fixed. These are diagnostic adjustments, not validated climate records.

citations.reason: Uses its signed regional monthly evidence. Tests sensitivity of regional step-trend attribution to gradual difference drift.
Extends the need to account for structural correction uncertainty; does not recompute its heatwave statistics.
